check.reason: Two problems. (1) The take cites 'an estimated 7.5 million people' affected by restrictions. That figure is not in the headline or summary we were given, so it is an invented or unsupported number presented as fact. The headline's 'subtracts enrollees elsewhere' claim is also not part of the real story, which is about approving traditional healing in two states, so it risks misstating the story. (2) It isn't satirical. The take is earnest policy commentary ('welcome expansion', 'real progress') with no joke, exaggeration, or deadpan absurdity aimed at the system. It does not target or mock patients, authors, or private individuals, but it fails on the unsupported number and the lack of satire. Rewrite it with no unsourced figures and an actual satirical angle on the bureaucracy or the administration's policy.

pick.title: Trump Administration OKs Native Traditional Healing for Two States’ Medicaid Programs
pick.headline: Administration Adds Medicaid Benefit in Two States, Subtracts Enrollees Elsewhere
pick.take: Approving traditional healing is a welcome expansion of what Medicaid covers. It arrives alongside restrictions that will affect access for an estimated 7.5 million people. Coverage for a new service is real progress, but it counts for less when the coverage itself is being cut back.
